transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

What finally made me come in is this constant tightness in my neck, shoulders, and jaw. It feels like I’m bracing for bad news all the time, even when I’m just at my desk or trying to watch TV at night.
How long have you been experiencing this constant tightness and feeling of bracing for bad news—days, weeks, or longer?
About seven months now. It started after a pipe burst and the remodeling turned the house upside down.
Besides the stress from the house repairs, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several other things in your life—like work, health, or family—even when there's no clear reason to?

Yes. My mind keeps jumping from the contractors maybe missing something in the house to whether my lesson plans are slipping, whether the robotics kids are falling behind, and whether I’m letting my wife and family down by not keeping things under control.
When these worries about the house, your job, or your family start, how hard is it for you to stop or control them once they begin?

It’s very hard to stop. I’ll tell myself to focus on the class in front of me, but then something small—an invoice that’s late or a student falling behind—starts this whole chain of what-ifs. Once it gets going, I can’t seem to shut it down.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep—trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested—since this worrying began?
I’m not really sure I’ve noticed a clear change in my sleep.
Have you noticed that it's harder to concentrate on tasks, or that you're more irritable than usual, since this worrying began?

Yes, I think so. I’ve been falling behind on lesson prep and grading, which isn’t like me. And I had to give up some of the community-theater work I usually handle because I just couldn’t keep up with everything.
